Thought of the week U.S. inflation remains elevated, with price pressures extending beyond energy into a wider range of goods and services. Core CPI rose 0.3% for the third consecutive month in Oct, highlighting the persistence of underlying inflation. Shelter remained the largest contributor, while transportation, recreation and medical care services also added to price pressures. Meanwhile, higher energy and import costs, alongside the delayed effects of earlier tariffs, are gradually filtering through to consumer prices as businesses seek to recover rising operating expenses. Although moderating wage growth may provide some relief, the lagged impact of earlier cost increases could keep inflation elevated even as the initial energy shock fades. Looking ahead, broadening price pressures across goods and services may complicate the Federal Reserve’s path towards its 2% inflation target.

items.title: Jay Clayton to act as national cyber director until Kirsten Davies confirmed
items.excerpt: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will also serve as acting national cyber director while Kirsten Davies awaits Senate confirmation to lead the office, Axios has learned. - A White House official said the strong support Davies received convinced Trump to nominate her to lead the office permanently rather than keep her in an acting capacity. Why it matters: Clayton, the nation's top intelligence official, will now coordinate cybersecurity policy as outages and reported cyberattacks expose vulnerabilities in America's digital infrastructure. Catch up quick: President Trump announced Thursday he was tapping Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, to replace Sean Cairncross as national cyber director. - Davies will assist Clayton as a senior adviser in the Office of the National Cyber Director until she is confirmed. ... The big picture: Two critical national security roles will temporarily fall under one official as President Trump shakes up his cybersecurity team amid the growing threat of AI-powered attacks. - The disruptions have raised concerns about the vulnerability of the nation's digital infrastructure, although administration officials say there is no evidence they were caused by coordinated cyberattacks. - Clayton himself has played a prominent role in the administration's response, telling lawmakers Wednesday that the outages appeared to stem from unrelated technical problems and system upgrades.

items.title: 'White Blast' tops box office in first weekend | Yonhap News Agency
items.excerpt: All News 10:52 November 23, 2026 SEOUL, Nov. 23 (Yonhap) -- The Korean film "White Blast" debuted at No. 1 at the local box office, attracting more than 300,000 moviegoers in its first weekend. The film garnered 310,000 admissions from Friday to Sunday, accounting for 39.6 percent of ticket sales at theaters nationwide, according to the Korean Film Council on Monday. Released Nov. 18, "White Blast" is a black comedy thriller set at a remote train station isolated by heavy snow. It follows retiring station master Gap-soo (Kim Yoon-seok) and his successor Hyun-taek (Koo Kyo-hwan) as they discover a body inside a railway tunnel while on patrol and grow suspicious of each other. It was co-directed by Hong Eui-jeong, known for "Voice of Silence" (2020), and newbie director Park Sun-woo. ... The Japanese animated film "Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island," which had held the No. 1 spot for six consecutive weeks through the previous weekend, fell to second place with around 91,000 admissions. Its cumulative attendance reached about 3 million, making it the most-viewed animated film released this year. "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," the latest installment in "The Hunger Games" series, ranked third with around 59,000 admissions, while the survival film "Fall 2: Deadpoint" placed fourth with about 53,000 admissions. Singer Lim Young-woong's concert film "Lim Young Woong: Im Hero the Stadium 2" rounded out the top five with around 31,000 admissions.

items.excerpt: ### Clashing Through The Snow PG-13 In this romantic comedy, a holiday snowstorm strands rival publishing editors Ryan Mitchell (Christopher Briney) and Hannah Hendricks (Michelle Randolph) at the airport, forcing them into a shared rental car for a cross-country race to New York.
